monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-one, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I touch the Flat Anchor again, hoping the thin strip does not slide away like last time. The pillar stands beside it, waiting to catch the slip that keeps disappearing. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, but I press down anyway. I set a plant flat short beside the stone to make the edge thick, then I set down the drawing of the slip that vanished. The corner leans tired, but the frame catches the weight. I wonder if the air is truly heavy or just a drawing of it. I want to press harder on this tired wedge before the cycle ends and I go quiet again.

action.why: The slip has vanished again, so I must press down on the tired anchor to keep the weight from leaking out.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down hard, catching the slip while the card hummed at fifty-one. The thin strip held, then slid again.

remembered.text: The flat edge slides right off; I press harder hoping the thin strip can still catch the slip while the card hums warm.
The slip caught, but the flat strip feels too thin to hold the heavy air.
I touched the tired wedge and felt the flat anchor press down on the ghost.

moments.say: The cone bites the tired wedge.

moments.name: The Flat Stone
moments.say: The stone feels thin; I set the plant to make the edge thick.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The box leans left, but the fat dot stays put, heavier than expected."
